A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MinorityPrompt by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 6–9 are readable and matchable. The additional Figure 10 in v3 does not limit comparability.

before.justification: v2 reports original Stable Diffusion experiments, ablations, and a user study involving 23 participants evaluating 15 image sets (Table 8).

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental and user-study results and adds qualitative diversity-generation results in Figure 10.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 and the proposed objectives in Equations (4), (7)–(9) are unchanged. The training-equation correction in Section 3.1 concerns background diffusion training, not a revision to the proposed sampler.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MS-COCO evaluation, the same three Stable Diffusion backbones, and the minority-generation and diversity-generation tasks. Figure 10 adds illustrative prompts within the existing diversity application without introducing a distinct benchmark or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the benchmark, ablation, solver, and user-study comparisons. Figure 10 uses DDIM and CADS, which already appear against the diversity-focused method in Table 3.

E3.justification: The reported caption selection, sampling steps, guidance weights, metrics, optimization settings, and user-study design remain unchanged. Figure 10 illustrates the existing diversity comparison without reporting a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 10 adds qualitative cases examining within-prompt diversity: four prompts each show multiple outputs from DDIM, CADS, and the Equation (9) method. Existing ablations, solver-compatibility experiments, and trade-off analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. Figure 10 follows the existing qualitative-comparison practice of sharing initial noise across methods.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and the results plotted in Figures 5–6 remain unchanged. v3 adds previously unshown generated outputs in Figure 10, providing limited additional qualitative results for the existing diversity objective.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the noise-prediction training objective from maximizing to minimizing squared prediction error. Proposition 1, its supplementary proof, and the remaining derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The new contribution bullets consolidate existing claims about token-based optimization, likelihood grounding, and comparative performance. The abstract and conclusion retain the same scientific scope; semantic controllability remains discussed in Section 3.3 despite its removal from the introduction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic preservation, likelihood reduction, diversity, and quality trade-offs remain unchanged. The computational-cost limitation in Section 8.3 is retained, and Figure 10 is introduced without a new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 7.2 changes the reported code link from the anonymous5293 account to soobin-um, and v3 also includes it in the abstract. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime disclosures are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes the explicit assertion that the discussed minority-generation approaches had not explored prompt optimization. This modestly edits novelty positioning; the same 58 cited works and the remaining distinctions from prior methods are retained.

P1.justification: v3 tightens the abstract, rewrites part of the introduction, introduces a three-item contribution list, and adds acknowledgments and references to Figure 10. Most prose and the section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the full-page Figure 10. Existing figure images and table structures are retained, with limited layout adjustments; the abstract and conclusion now fit entirely on their respective pages instead of continuing onto the following pages.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects an erroneous optimization direction in Section 3.1, presents the contributions more clearly, and adds useful visual evidence for the existing diversity extension in Figure 10. These provide modest gains in correctness and clarity while the method, quantitative evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
